g_policy.reason: The card is opt-in and the offer copy states the reward (3 Advanced reasoning mode answers today). The 'Not now' decline leaves home unchanged, and if_the_ad_fails covers both no game available and an unconfirmed play.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 3 Advanced reasoning mode answers that expire at midnight, so it has no cash value.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is the first app open after 3 or more days with no session, which is an app event and needs no chat content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The proposal adds no cap and removes nothing free (removes nothing free: yes). It only adds a sample of a paid feature.

g_brand_safety.reason: The offer is a dismissible card under the header on s01 Chats home, which is rated safe. It is app chrome and is not placed in a conversation.

c1_revealed_value.reason: Advanced reasoning mode is a paywall bullet (l02, s02.e03), so the app charges for the resource the reward gives.

c2_evidence.reason: The 'what makes it work here' field says 'Luzia also plays a 15-second video ad before every fifth answer, so free users are already used to ads.' No mechanic or element in the product model shows this, and the model lists no free-tier limit or ad behavior, so this claim about the app today is unsupported.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The sample is 3 answers and ends at midnight, so it is a limited, expiring taste. The full feature stays behind the paid plans and it takes nothing from other users.

c5_moment.reason: The card shows at app open on the home screen, so it does not interrupt a task in progress.

c6_fits_simula.reason: It is a play-to-earn unit, and the reward is granted after a confirmed play ('If the play isn't confirmed... try again'). The trigger, a first open after a 3+ day gap, is detectable by the app.

c7_specific.reason: It names Luzia's 'Advanced reasoning mode' paywall feature, the Luzia+ badge on Chats home, and the 'How can I help you today?' prompt card.

other_concern: The rationale says each answer uses real model time and that the offer pays for itself in higher-earning markets. These are predictions and were not checked. The 'when the reward runs out' note also adds a new trial prompt, which is a proposal addition and not a claim about the app today.
